title: The Hollow Static
premise: Freya Thornbury smuggles forbidden memories through orbital customs aboard her ship, the Hollow Static, carrying the recorded last days of Meridian Colony—a settlement the war's victors erased from every archive. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, Freya experiences a vision of the colony's true fate: it was destroyed to hide a jump-drive discovery that could end the war. Hunted by both fleets, she must deliver the colony's final message to the enemy flagship before the next jump window closes, forcing her to choose between selling the truth and giving it away. She broadcasts the memory publicly, ending the war but losing her ship, her cargo, and the quiet anonymity that kept her alive.
about_author: Yara Joubert is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from displaced communities before turning to fiction. They write science fiction about what survives when institutions decide what deserves to be remembered.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Freya runs a memory-capsule shipment past orbital customs at Ceres Gate, using her dead mother's forged credentials. POV: Freya. The beat is competence masking grief—she's good at this, and being good at it has cost her everyone she loves.

chapters.title: The Colony That Wasn't
chapters.summary: A dying client pays Freya in unregistered memories: the final days of Meridian Colony, which officially never existed. POV: Freya, with intercut memory-POV of Meridian engineer Dov Askeland. The emotional beat is vertigo—she realizes the archives themselves are contraband.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Gravity flickers across the entire system for exactly nine seconds; ships drift, stations groan, and Freya relives Meridian's destruction as if she were there. POV: Freya. The beat is terror and revelation: the flicker wasn't an accident—it was a message, and she's the only one who received it whole.

chapters.title: Customs Comes Knocking
chapters.summary: Orbital customs officer Ilsa Reyes boards the Hollow Static hunting whoever decoded the flicker. Freya hides the capsule inside her own neural implant. POV: alternating Freya and Reyes, who suspects but hesitates. The beat is cat-and-mouse intimacy—two women who both serve systems they no longer believe in.

chapters.title: What the Victor Kept
chapters.summary: Freya traces the flicker's origin to a derelict relay near Meridian's coordinates and finds evidence the colony discovered a stable jump corridor—worth more than either fleet's entire navy. POV: Freya. The beat is corrupted wonder: power doesn't want peace; it wants monopoly.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: A black-market broker offers Freya fortune and protection if she sells the corridor data to the winning side. Her oldest friend, Tam, takes the deal and betrays her location. POV: Freya, then Tam. The beat is heartbreak—the inheritance theme turns bitter: we become what we're handed.

chapters.title: Burn Vector
chapters.summary: Pursued by both fleets, Freya makes a desperate burn toward the enemy flagship, guided by Dov's recorded voice and shadowed by Reyes, who defects to help her. POV: Freya and Reyes. The beat is reluctant hope—trust rebuilt mid-flight, with torpedoes falling behind them.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Aboard the enemy flagship, Freya plays Meridian's final message: not coordinates or weapons, but the colonists' names, faces, and last words—an inheritance of grief neither fleet can weaponize cleanly. POV: Freya. The beat is devastating stillness; soldiers weep at consoles built for targeting.

chapters.title: Before the Window Closes
chapters.summary: The admiralties move to seize the corridor anyway; with minutes left in the jump window, Freya broadcasts the full Meridian record on open channels, making the truth public property. POV: Freya, Reyes, and fleet officers reacting. The beat is climax—power corrupts, but publicity disarms it.

chapters.title: After Static
chapters.summary: The ceasefire holds because neither side can claim Meridian without claiming its ghosts. Freya, stripped of ship and cargo, opens a small archive where anyone can deposit their dead. POV: Freya, closing with Dov's voice. The beat is quiet resolution: memory outlives power when it's given, not sold.
